requirements.malformed: each family has a truncated length-delimited negative fixture
requirements.unknown_field: each family has a legal field 19000 varint fixture accepted by decoders
requirements.map_order: Account contains equivalent maps in distinct entry order
requirements.presence: Transaction.raw distinguishes absent timestamp from explicitly encoded default
requirements.any: extension Any preserves canonical type URL and value bytes
requirements.size: every fixture records exact encoded size and SHA-256
requirements.rust_raw_wire: all fixtures decode through generated Rust types behind a boundary retaining exact original bytes
requirements.rust_constructed_maps: map-bearing constructed messages use the public bounded insertion-ordered encoder and reproduce protobuf-java entry order
requirements.java_constructed_maps: protobuf-java 3.25.8 DynamicMessage outputs cover forward and reverse insertion for every descriptor map field

rust_encoding_decision.raw_inbound: hash, signature, network, and API relay paths emit retained original bytes exactly, including unknown fields, explicit defaults, duplicate fields, and original map-entry order
rust_encoding_decision.mutation: decoded messages are immutable while preservation applies; mutation or construction consumes/leaves the preservation boundary and requires explicit constructed encoding
rust_encoding_decision.constructed: constructed map-bearing messages use the public bounded insertion-ordered encoder; direct prost Message::encode is non-compatible and forbidden at observable boundaries
rust_encoding_decision.java_distinction: constructed-message determinism does not claim Java raw-byte preservation; only retained inbound bytes provide byte identity
rust_encoding_decision.java_constructed: the ordered API reproduces Java forward insertion bytes and Java reverse insertion bytes for all 15 descriptor map fields; retained raw inbound bytes remain exact
rust_encoding_decision.direct_encode: direct prost Message::encode for constructed map-bearing messages is not a Java-compatibility encoding API and must not be used where bytes are observable
